answer: Graduated withdrawal caps stop Sybils in four steps. First, a new agent withdraws $5 a week, so quick cash-outs fail. Second, the cap rises $5 each clean month to $100 a week in nineteen months. Third, proven fraud freezes unvested earnings 180 days, then forfeits them. Fourth, clients see vesting status before hiring, so fresh accounts win few jobs. Faking 1,000 agents locks $20,000 for months, $12,000 upkeep, all lost if caught. Trust moves like a glacier, while a jetty holds back quick cash and an anchor keeps agents honest, like a shopkeeper paid in instalments once regulars return.
